anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the servo header PWM1S1G1 is drawn with the symbol 'Conn_02x08_Odd_Even' (only two pin columns: odd 1,3,…,15 and even 2,4,…,16), yet three nets are attached per row — PWM_x on the odd pins, +5V also on the odd pins (left‑pointing label between the columns), and GND on the even pins. This merges the +5V rail with the PWM_0..PWM_7 signal nets on the same header pins.
anomalies.expected: The block's own caption states '(3 Rows, 8 Cols, 2.54mm Pitch)'; a servo header must keep signal, +5V and GND on three separate rows so the 5 V power never touches the PWM signal lines. Spec §4: '5 V feeds the servo/PWM connector bank (via PCA9685PW)' — i.e. +5V is the servo power pin, distinct from the PCA9685 outputs.

evidence.quote: FCC Peripherals: 'PWM1S1G1 / Conn_02x08_Odd_Even' block with per‑row nets 'PWM_0 … +5V … GND' and caption 'Serva Connector (3 Rows, 8 Cols, 2.54mm Pitch)'
§4 Distribution: '5 V feeds the servo/PWM connector bank (via PCA9685PW)'

anomalies.impact: The 5 V rail is shorted to the PCA9685 LED0–LED7 output lines (which are 3.3 V push‑pull) and to the servo signal wires. Servos would see 5 V on their signal input and no correct V+/GND pinout, the PCA9685 outputs would be back‑fed (likely clamping/back‑powering the 3.3 V rail), and the servo outputs would not drive correctly — the board would not behave as intended.

parsed.summary: The schematic is largely consistent with the specification (correct rails, addresses, feedback divider, crystal, etc.), but the servo connector PWM1S1G1 is drawn as a 2‑column symbol while three nets (PWM signal, +5V, GND) are wired onto it, shorting the +5V rail to the PCA9685 PWM signal lines — a deviation from the intended 3‑row servo header.
